title: Redwood discovery - model selection: Meridian Edge
summary: Discovery focused on model selection for Meridian Edge's multilingual customer support and knowledge base assistant. Discussed context length needs (up to 32k), tool-calling/function calling, hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs, security requirements (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM), and benchmarking next steps. Agreed to run a 2-week POC: Redwood will run latency/cost benchmarks on candidate open models and provide security docs and pricing; Meridian Edge will share sample prompts and access patterns.
topics: open model comparisons (Redwood-Base, Mistral, Llama variants)
deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem)
security/compliance: SOC 2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
latency vs cost tradeoffs and batching
next_steps: Redwood to share security packet (SOC2/ISO docs) and KMS/HSM architecture notes
SE to run benchmark using Meridian Edge prompt set and return latency/cost matrix within 7 business days
Schedule technical deep-dive (POC scoping) for next Tuesday 2026-12-14 10:00 PT
Send pricing + Dedicated capacity options and estimated commit tiers
action_items: Priya (SE): request sample prompt set and traffic profile from David/Nina - due 2026-12-09
Jared (AE): send security packet and SSO/SAML integration guide - due 2026-12-08
Meridian Edge (David): provide anonymized KB dump + sample session traces - due 2026-12-10
Priya (SE): run 1st-pass benchmarks (hosted + dedicated variants) and share results - due 2026-12-15
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-06 14:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Jared, Priya (Redwood); Carol, David, Nina, Tom (Meridian Edge)

[00:00] Jared (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Carol (CTO): yep carol here, cto at meridian edge, we run a customer support assistant and internal knowledge search.
[00:14] David (ML Eng): david, ml eng, i'm leading the model eval and infra side.
[00:20] Jared (AE): cool, i'm jared at redwood, and priya is our solutions engineer who will take us through the technical bits.
[00:27] Priya (SE): hi all, hi carol, david, nina, tom. quick agenda: understand your requirements (context length, languages, tool calling), talk model candidates and deployment modes, then next steps.
[00:36] Nina (Product): our main use case is a chat assistant for support — multi-lingual (en/es/jp), sometimes long transcripts from support cases so we need long context.
[00:46] Tom (Infra): we care about data residency and compliance. we currently run in aws, vpc enabled, and have a strict sso/saml setup.
[00:53] Priya (SE): noted. what's your typical session length and token counts?
[00:56] David: average session 1.5k tokens but we have edge cases up to 25k tokens — the KB articles can be long; planning for up to 32k to be safe.
[01:07] Jared: great, so long-context models matter. we can talk about models with native 32k context and strategies for prefixing, kv cache usage, or retrieval augmentation.
[01:18] Carol: we also need tool-calling — function calls to our ticketing system, and structured json output for routing.
[01:25] Priya: Redwood supports tool-calling and structured outputs; our runtime preserves function arguments and we can stream partial results. one note: some open models have patchy function calling behavior; our SEs test specific model variants.
[01:38] David: interested in open models to avoid vendor lock and control costs — we've been looking at Mistral, Llama2/3 variants, and some smaller Redwood-profiles. what's your opinion?
[01:48] Priya: Mistral does well on instruction-following and is cost-efficient, Llama3 large variants give good quality but can be more costly; Redwood-Base (our curated open checkpoint) is tuned for production latency/costs. context-length support varies — Llama3 has 32k variants, Mistral has some long-context forks but less tested.
[02:06] Tom: about deployment: what are the pros/cons of hosted vs dedicated vs private? we prefer VPC with customer-managed keys.
[02:13] Jared: hosted is fastest to get started and we provide model catalog + streaming API; dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput for steady traffic; private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control over networking and KMS/HSM integration. If data residency and key control are must-haves, private or dedicated with VPC peering is the common path.
[02:32] Nina: latency expectations? sub-200ms per token ideally for interactive UI.
[02:37] Priya: sub-200ms is aggressive depending on model size and context; with quantized 8-bit execution and good batching you can get interactive latencies on smaller models. for 32k context, cache warmup and streaming matter — we recommend smart caching and a fall back to a smaller model for low latency paths.
[02:55] David: what's the batching behavior? our traffic is spiky during business hours.
[02:58] Priya: runtime supports continuous batching and workload-aware batching policies; we can tune target latency percentiles vs throughput. Dedicated pools let you cap concurrency to avoid noisy neighbor issues.
[03:10] Carol: security — do you have SOC2 and can we integrate with our SAML SSO? also audit logs?
[03:16] Jared: yes SOC2 Type II and ISO certs available in the security packet we'll share. we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations for private deployments. for hosted we can integrate customer-managed keys via BYOK in certain regions; for private you bring your own key material into the environment.
[03:33] Tom: HSM support?
[03:35] Priya: yes, HSM-backed KMS is supported for private deployments, and we can document key rotation procedures.
[03:41] David: benchmarking — what will you measure? latency, throughput, cost per 1k tokens?
[03:45] Priya: we'll run a benchmark matrix: candidate models across your sample prompt set, measuring p50/p95 latency, average cost per 1k tokens, and quality metrics (rate of correct function calls/structured outputs). will include hosted baseline and dedicated variants.
[03:58] Carol: do you do multilingual evals?
[04:00] Priya: yes we'll include EN/ES/JP prompts and measure hallucination rates in each language. some models are stronger in english; others like Llama3 have improved multilinguality.
[04:10] David: are there limitations around long-context for embeddings or retrieval?
[04:13] Priya: embeddings are separate; we recommend chunking for retrieval and using a hybrid approach: dense embeddings + sparse retrieval and then use retrieval-augmented generation. for true 32k context we can patch models with sliding window or KV-caching to avoid re-encoding huge histories.
[04:28] Jared: tradeoffs: bigger models with longer context cost more and increase latency; smaller models plus retrieval can be cheaper and equally accurate for KB style tasks.
[04:38] Nina: about pricing — can you share a cost estimate for a 1M monthly token volume with mixed read/write?
[04:44] Jared: we'll send a pricing sheet; rough ballpark depends on model choice and deployment. Dedicated reserved commit can lower unit cost significantly versus hosted pay-as-you-go.
[04:54] Tom: any known issues with tool-calling and streaming? we've had problems with partial function args being truncated.
[04:59] Priya: streaming + function args is supported but you need to ensure your client buffers correctly; for partial args we prefer atomic argument emission—Redwood's runtime can ensure function call integrity and we surface incomplete calls as explicit flags. we'll test with your ticketing integration during the POC.
[05:17] David: network egress/data residency — if we do hosted, will data leave our VPC/region?
[05:23] Jared: hosted is region-aware but it's shared infra; for strict residency choose private or dedicated in your region. we can provide dedicated capacity in a single AZ/region with VPC peering.
[05:33] Nina: timeline — we're targeting a Q1 roll-out and want a POC in january.
[05:37] Jared: that works. propose a 2-week POC starting mid-december or early january.
[05:43] Carol: who are the stakeholders? cto and product for success criteria, procurement for contracts.
[05:48] Jared: noted. success criteria?
[05:50] Nina: accuracy >= 92% on intent detection, p95 latency < 500ms for 90% of queries, cost less than $0.0005 per token average for inference.
[06:03] Priya: good concrete targets — we'll measure and report.
[06:06] Jared: ok recap: priya will run benchmarks on candidate models (mistral, llama3-32k, redwood-base), include multilingual tests and tool-calling checks; we'll share security docs and a pricing sheet; meridian to share prompts and KB sample.
[06:23] David: do you support canary rollouts and automatic fallback (smaller model) in case of latency spikes?
[06:27] Priya: yes we have rollout policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; can set routing by latency or cost tiers.
[06:35] Carol: what about prompt evals and regression alerts?
[06:38] Jared: Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets — can surface drift or quality regressions and tie them to model rollouts.
[06:47] Tom: any pre-reqs for private deployment? hardware specs?
[06:50] Priya: for on-prem/private we provide an installer and recommend GPU types (A100/Tr4 equivalents) and network specs; we'll share the system requirements doc.
[06:58] Carol: ok next steps then.
[07:00] Jared: action items visible in the chat — we'll follow up. thanks all.
[07:04] Nina: thanks everyone.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-heards like "K-V cash" for KV cache and "V-P-C" spelled out; proper nouns sometimes inconsistent. References: 'security packet' link (to be sent), 'benchmark script' and 'pricing spreadsheet' to be shared.
